assumptions: VEB sparse multiple regression fitted by CAVI
conclusion: CAVI can converge slowly with correlated predictors and its sequential updates impede parallelization.
scope: Computational motivation for gradient-based VEB; no universal speed guarantee.
span: Following the most commonly-used approach in variational inference, [29] used coordinate ascent to optimize the variational objective function. The resulting “coordinate ascent variational inference" (CAVI) algorithm performed well in their numerical comparisons. However, CAVI has some important computational limitations. First, CAVI can be slow to converge in settings with correlated predictors (Figure 1). Second, because the CAVI algorithm, by design, updates one parameter at a time, holding all others fixed, it cannot be easily parallelized.
